newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices firm on Texas refinery speculation.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices firm on Texas refinery speculation.

text.p: Oil prices rose on Monday after talk of trouble at a giant Texas refinery ran through the market.

Traders in the United States suspected a problem at Amoco's Texas City refinery after the company bought as much as 300,000 barrels of gasoline on the spot market, presumably to cover lost output. Company officials were unavailable for comment
Gasoline on the U.S. spot market rose a healthy two cents a gallon, which pulled up the crude oil market on both sides of the Atlantic.
Benchmark North Sea Brent crude futures traded in London were up 26 cents at $24.48 a barrel at 1648 GMT.
Low stocks in the United States were seen as the reason for the market's sensitivity to any supply disruption.
"Inventories are extremely low," said consultant Gary Ross of the Petroleum Industry Research Associates. "The market is very vulnerable to surprises because there is no cushion."
Prices may rise even further before the end of the year, Ross told an industry conference in London.
